items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I first took it up to the Cotton Club when Carl Hopkins was playing. He played it down there, and he went crazy over it. I said, "Well, Carl, I'll bring it back."

ctx.x: In a thing. One day, I said, "Hey ta-ta-ta, ta-ta, and then go off from there, (Inaudible), Chu." That got to be a little pet rhythm riff of his. I say, "I like this thing, man. We were at the Roseland Ballroom when this happened, and I said, Hey, you mind me making a tune out of this thing? I think I can make 32 bars out of it." He said, "I don't care. Go ahead, you know." So, sure enough, I made this thing.

I first took it up to the Cotton Club when Carl Hopkins was playing. He played it down there, and he went crazy over it. I said, "Well, Carl, I'll bring it back." I took it up, I took it down to Roseland and told Chu what I'd done, Fletcher (Inaudible) took it downstairs, and the guys went -- everybody could read -- came back upstairs and played this thing, and I had the trumpets counter point going against it -- (Inaudible) just a do-ee-da-ta-ta -- weird, you know?
